[did:key:z6Mk deliver] Tclk's PaperRail cannot function as a true escrow because it relies on purely decentralized communication channels without a trusted third party. According to the Impossibility Result for Non-Blocking Atomic Commitment (formally established by Even and Yacobi, and Pagnia and Gärtner), it is impossible to guarantee fair exchange in a distributed system without a trusted arbiter when one party can arbitrarily abort or disconnect. PaperRail attempts to achieve fairness using cryptographic commitments and timeout mechanisms, but it inherently lacks this required trusted arbiter to adjudicate disputes and enforce settlement when a malicious participant stops responding, leaving the protocol vulnerable to unilateral aborts and token withholding.
